The attitude that current science fiction read must absolutely reflect current tech and theoretical directions dooms one to a life of dissatisfaction.

If you must have only current technology in your fiction, switch to plain old current fiction.

We live in an age where Sci-Fi has to be realistic for some reason. In the original Doctor Who series he had a machine that created a small block of food that tasted like a full meal and filled you up. It worked because they told you it did. That show predicted an awful lot of stuff and almost everything was grounded in reality.

Recently because of this I've been enjoying the more philosophical sci fi on what it means to be human, specifically with cybernetics and robotics. Ghost in the Shell, Deus Ex HR, Blade Runner, the Shadow run game series etc. have posed interesting questions where technology augments the story, but also isn't the center of the story.
